periods.public: The committee discusses which data sources will best inform their decision. They focus on cost accuracy, scheduling risks, user satisfaction, and staff workload.

lines.Mizuki: Suggests looking at user satisfaction and room usage.
lines.Victoria: Agrees and adds the need for timetable and booking data.
lines.Benjamin: Proposes checking delivery schedules and site diaries for delays.
lines.Kenji: Wants to see tender records and renewal reserves for cost clarity.
lines.Shunichi: Requests staffing posts and technician routines to assess labor.

lines.Mizuki: Confirms her choice of post-occupancy reviews and booking data.
lines.Victoria: Confirms her choice of timetable records and booking data.
lines.Benjamin: Confirms his choice of delivery schedules and site diaries.
lines.Kenji: Confirms his choice of tender records and renewal reserves.
lines.Shunichi: Confirms his choice of staffing posts and technician routines.

periods.public: Participants share the implications of their findings. They debate the risks of outdoor work, the inefficiency of current equipment, and the demand for general-purpose space.

lines.Mizuki: Notes that flexible, bookable spaces are rated highest by users.
lines.Victoria: Mentions that off-site hiring costs are a burden during works.
lines.Benjamin: Warns that outdoor projects are prone to weather delays.
lines.Kenji: Points out that mechanical costs are rising significantly.
lines.Shunichi: Highlights that technicians are doing manual work due to old gear.

lines.Mizuki: Asks @Victoria if booking data shows a shortage of general rooms.
lines.Victoria: Confirms that general rooms are overbooked while specialist ones are idle.
lines.Benjamin: Notes that comfort-based projects often slip in schedule.
lines.Kenji: Questions if there is money set aside for equipment replacement.
lines.Shunichi: Argues that the current staff cannot handle more manual routines.

lines.Mizuki: Suggests prioritizing high-demand, low-risk internal conversions.
lines.Victoria: Agrees that minimizing off-site displacement is key.
lines.Benjamin: Cautions against any project with high weather exposure.
lines.Kenji: Warns that mechanical upgrades will be expensive.
lines.Shunichi: Emphasizes the need to reduce the manual burden on technicians.

periods.public: The committee evaluates the four candidates against the gathered evidence. They weigh the trade-offs between urgent technical needs, user demand, and budget/schedule risks.

lines.Mizuki: Argues for the option that meets high general demand.
lines.Victoria: Agrees, noting it avoids the worst timetable disruptions.
lines.Benjamin: Notes it is an indoor project, avoiding weather risks.
lines.Kenji: Questions the cost of the conversion versus the upgrade.
lines.Shunichi: Argues that the technical upgrade is a necessity for staff.

lines.Mizuki: Counters that the general space serves more people.
lines.Victoria: Points out the inefficiency of the specialist rooms.
lines.Benjamin: Warns that the technical upgrade might slip in schedule.
lines.Kenji: Notes the rising cost of mechanical plant lots.
lines.Shunichi: Insists that staff burnout is a critical risk.

lines.Mizuki: Suggests the conversion is the safest and most popular bet.
lines.Victoria: Agrees with the logic of maximizing utility.
lines.Benjamin: Concedes that the conversion has the lowest risk profile.
lines.Kenji: Acknowledges the budget risk of the mechanical option.
lines.Shunichi: Maintains that the technical need is urgent but acknowledges the demand.

seats.Kenji: Concerned with budget accuracy and hidden costs. He analyzes the financial data to see if the proposed works are realistic.
seats.Benjamin: Concerned with scheduling and external delays. He evaluates projects based on their likelihood of being completed on time.
seats.Mizuki: Concerned with user satisfaction and actual utility. She looks for evidence of what the campus community truly needs.
seats.Victoria: Concerned with operational disruption and space efficiency. She focuses on how works affect the daily timetable.
seats.Shunichi: Concerned with staff workload and maintenance burdens. He advocates for improvements that reduce manual labor for technicians.
